node: Defense subtier components and qualified industrial suppliers
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: This pass expands the universe for qualified lower-tier defense/aerospace suppliers rather than primes. The strongest reference anchor is TransDigm because its public filings explicitly frame it as a proprietary aerospace-component supplier with meaningful defense exposure. The underfollowed discovery lane is more interesting in smaller suppliers such as Ducommun, Park Aerospace, and Hexcel, where exposure is embedded in aerostructures, electromechanical systems, composites, rocket-motor materials, radomes, military aircraft, space, and launch programs. These names map to the bottleneck hypothesis because they sit below prime contractors, require qualified manufacturing processes, and may be constrained by program-specific certifications, materials, lead times, customer-directed sources, and uneven defense demand. No buy/sell recommendation is implied. Layer 1B expands the defense-subtier supplier node into a compact two-lane universe. The reference lane uses TransDigm as a visible benchmark for proprietary, hard-to-substitute aerospace and defense components. The underfollowed lane prioritizes smaller US-listed manufacturers whose public labels are industrial, aerospace materials, electronics, or engineered-products rather than pure-play defense primes. The chokepoint hypothesis remains that DoD and prime-contractor demand may be constrained by qualified processes, certified production, long program qualification cycles, cleared or controlled work, and supplier willingness to carry uneven defense volumes.
